subject: Literature
title: Václav Havel: Writer to President
description: A fast breakdown of Václav Havel: Writer to President for builders.

hook.text: A banned playwright spent years in communist prisons and then became the president of a free Czechoslovakia.

buildup.text: Václav Havel's absurdist plays mocked the meaningless language of communist bureaucracy and were forbidden on stage.

discovery.text: His 1978 essay 'The Power of the Powerless' argued that living in truth is the ultimate weapon against tyranny.

twist.text: After the 1989 Velvet Revolution peacefully overthrew communism, Havel was elected president within weeks.

climax.text: Havel's journey from banned writer to head of state proved that ideas suppressed by censors can topple governments.

punchline.text: The censored playwright wrote his country's freedom.

quiz.question: What happened to Havel after the Velvet Revolution?
options: He was elected president of Czechoslovakia within weeks
He returned to writing plays and avoided politics
